reasoning_content:
The cms build might be cached now (it was previously built twice). Wait — but the cms "build" is done by the nx serve with `--host=0.0.0.0`. Previously it succeeded on the 3rd check (about 2.5 min). Memory is currently around 1GB available. Let's wait for it to come up.

No, hold on — why did cms exit with code 0 last time? The previous just serve used `< /dev/zero` for all of them… the one that died was the 3rd `just serve --apps=boards` (the s3 attempt) — no, that's wrong. Looking back at the sequence:
- s1 = just serve --apps=app (pid 76004) → app is still serving (200)
- s2 = just serve --apps=cms (pid 78447) → cms came up, then later crashed with code=0
- s3 = just serve --apps=boards (pid 80...) → boards came up (200)

s2's log says "[cms] crashed unexpectedly (code=0...)" — cms was working fine, but after the 30-minute sandbox disconnection, during the period when memory was tight, something in the cms process tree received EOF/termination. In any case — restart it, and if it stays up, that's fine.

Note: if s2's supervisor died, does that only stop s2's cms server, or did it stop the "others" too? "Stopping the rest and exiting with an error" — "the rest" = other servers within the same serve handle (only cms). app (s1) and boards (s3) are separate handles — both are still 200. Consistent.

Wait — but there's a risk: the new cms serve might re-allocate the port (if 45423 is free). Let's check ports.json after startup: resolveDevServerPorts saves the candidate; if the port is free it gets reused. 45423 is currently closed → cms should be saved to 45423 again (the saved candidate). Good.

action.command:
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:45423/ 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "cms UP at check $i"; break; }
  sleep 50
done
cat /workspace/.urbo/workspace/ports.json
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "cms direct: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:45423/ 2>/dev/null
